tldr: Evening batch (Sep 14): the frontier-pacing argument turned into written commitments. Sam Altman said OpenAI now writes a safety case before any frontier RL run expected to lift capability — moving its gate from release to development — and that he will not wait for legislation or an antitrust exemption before continuing; Nadella endorsed 'deliberate pacing' and Microsoft put a draft Code of Conduct for its MAI models into public consultation, with The Information reporting OpenAI, Anthropic and Google have been negotiating a shared oversight body. DeepSeek reversed itself: the V4-Pro retirement announced Sep 9 for 04:00 UTC today was cancelled about 45 hours later, and its pricing page now says V4-Pro service continues at unchanged billing — the load-bearing footnote being that the legacy flash ids are still accepted but served by V4.1-Flash at Flash prices, so a config pinned to the old name silently runs the new architecture. Hardware: Nvidia listed the RTX PRO 5500 Blackwell — 84GB of ECC GDDR7, 1,398 GB/s, 600W, the exact 21,760 CUDA-core count of a 5090, MIG-splittable into two isolated 42GB instances — the new middle rung between 72GB and 96GB, still 'Coming Soon' with no price. Governance: Narayanan and Kapoor argue liability should attach to the operator rather than the model, including in internal evals where safeguards were deliberately switched off. Open weights went sovereign and public-interest — Bodhan AI and NVIDIA shipped four open Indic ASR, OCR, MT and TTS models for India's Bharat EduAI Stack, and Humanity AI's $10M open call scores open-weight implementations above closed ones. On the local front a Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ4_XS build now holds ~100 tok/s decode across two R9700s and 128GB of RAM, and a 3D explainer makes V4.1-Flash's departure from a decode-only transformer visible.
